e: From Osnaburg, the former English name of the German city of Osnabrück (from which it may have been first imported into English-speaking countries).
q: [I]f he attended those solemn meetings at which the price of freight or the quality of Osnaburghs was discussed, he turned the venerable persons of the old merchants and grocers into ridicule […].
1791, Charlotte Smith, Celestina, Broadview, published 2004, page 258:
So that winter morning, I put on my osnaburg shirt and pants.
